problem:
Consider the set $B,$ defined as

$$
B={{b}_{n}\,:\,{b}_{n+2}={b}_{n+1}+{b}_{n}\,,\,{b}_{1}=3,\,{b}_{2}=1,\,n\in N}.
$$

Which of the following sets is equivalent to $B?$

feedback.problem:
Consider the set $B,$ defined as

$$
B={{b}_{n}\,:\,{b}_{n+2}={b}_{n+1}+{b}_{n}\,,\,{b}_{1}=0,\,{b}_{2}=3,\,n\in N}.
$$

Which of the following sets is equivalent to $B?$
feedback.worked_solution:
The elements of $B$ are all the terms of the *recursive* sequence ${b}_{n},$ given by

$$
{b}_{n+2}={b}_{n+1}+{b}_{n},\,{b}_{1}=0,\,{b}_{2}=3,\,n\in N.
$$

Notice that this is a Fibonacci sequence with ${b}_{1}=0$ and ${b}_{2}=3.$

Let's write down the first few terms of our sequence:

$$
\begin{aligned}{b}_{1} & =0 \\ {b}_{2} & =3 \\ {b}_{3} & ={b}_{2}+{b}_{1} \\  & =3+0 \\  & =3 \\ {b}_{4} & ={b}_{3}+{b}_{2} \\  & =3+3 \\  & =6 \\ {b}_{5} & ={b}_{4}+{b}_{3} \\  & =6+3 \\  & =9 \\ {b}_{6} & ={b}_{5}+{b}_{4} \\  & =9+6 \\  & =15 \\  & ⋮\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, 

$$
B={0,3,3,6,9,15,…}={0,3,6,9,15,…}.
$$
